svg.title: Nouns, rules, theorems
svg.desc: Three tiers. 1 Nouns: architecture.csf declares the proc gateway, the relay_inboxes service and a proposed process boundary; csfc in OCaml parses, decodes, type-checks and checks them against the Go source, emitting typed facts that serve as axioms. 2 Rules: rules.dl, typed by the nouns, holds call_lifetime and a typed CS-16 rule. 3 Theorems: Lean 4 states axioms emitted by csfc and proves that an empty call_lifetime relation means every in-process call is safe; the verifier stub today returns notImplemented. A Datalog summary closes the figure.
svg.text: Nouns, rules, theorems: who builds what
CSF and csfc define the nouns and check them against the code. Datalog says how they may play. Lean proves both are sound.
Nouns · CSF says what things are; csfc (OCaml) checks they ARE that
its typed output is the set of axioms everything above stands on

text.tspan: % then checked against the Go source

svg.text: an axiom = a declaration csfc checked against the code
trust rests on the source check: syntax-based, method calls unresolved today
Rules · Datalog says how the nouns may play

text.tspan: % a finding relation should stay empty; that emptiness is what Lean proves

svg.text: every constant is a declared noun
same rules: csfc, house lint, miners
Theorems · Lean proves the definitions sound, then proves the rules hold over them

text.tspan: -- a. the definitions are sound: consistent and well-formed
-- b. the rules hold: no finding means every in-process call is safe
-- the proof reasons over the Datalog program, never the OCaml

svg.text: b. the rules hold over them
OCaml builds the axioms it may use
today's stub aims at the compiler itself
this aims it at definitions and rules
